Use protected apps and sites intentionally

Voward adds a planning pause and clear time limits before selected apps and websites. It is a private self-management tool—not medical treatment or a diagnostic device. If digital use causes significant distress, sleep loss, unsafe behavior, or loss of control, consider seeking help from a qualified mental-health professional.

1. Review the disclosure, then grant only the permissions you accept.
2. Choose restricted apps from the installed-app picker and add domain/path rules for sites.
3. Set a daily allowance in minutes and a default planned session.
4. Create a recovery key, then choose the deactivation cooldown and how long you will have to confirm deactivation afterward.
5. At each gate, write a purpose, choose a duration, wait, and confirm again.
6. Review whether sessions ended early or reached their limit; adjust gradually.

One allowance second always buys one second of restricted use. The balance carries at most one daily allowance and can never fall below zero or borrow from a future day. When today’s allowance is depleted, no new restricted session can start. The re-entry pause grows logarithmically with sessions; it never changes a quoted session cap. Domain rules match the domain and subdomains. A path matches only that path and its subtree; a configured query must match exactly. Use keyword:text only when broad text matching is intentional.

The recovery key is the only in-app way to deactivate active protection. With a positive cooldown, enter it once to request deactivation and again during the deactivation confirmation period. Protection remains active while waiting. The optional uninstall guard adds friction but cannot turn a normal Android installation into an unbreakable kiosk. Accessibility can observe foreground app/window content and supported browser address text. Data stays on-device unless you explicitly export it.

1. Set a daily allowance, a default session length, and a real-life goal.
2. Choose at least one protected app or website.
3. Enable the required Attention Firewall accessibility service. Device Admin uninstall protection and notifications are optional.
4. Create a recovery key, then choose the deactivation cooldown and how long you will have to confirm deactivation afterward.
5. Review the setup summary and activate protection.

At the gate, name a specific purpose and choose 1–60 minutes. Start the circular pause, then review the plan and explicitly choose Open intentionally or Not now. Finishing the timer never opens protected content automatically. You can configure three alternatives in Settings; choosing one leaves the protected content, returns you Home, and is counted in Progress.

One allowance second buys one second of approved protected use. A session ends at the smaller of its planned duration or the allowance remaining when it starts. Unused allowance carries forward only up to one daily allowance, and the balance never becomes negative. Repeat entries increase only the next pause; they do not change the cost of a quoted session.

The Progress tab shows measured protected-use time, sessions, early exits, limits reached, the most common session start time, and the most frequently chosen alternative for the current week. Completed daily summaries are kept locally for up to 14 days. Voward does not estimate time saved or infer wellbeing, urges, or health outcomes.

Choose apps from the installed-app picker. For websites, example.com covers that domain and subdomains; example.com/news covers that path and its subtree; and a configured query must match exactly. Use keyword:shorts only for an intentionally broad match. A strict rule stays blocked regardless of remaining allowance. While protection is active, rules can only become more restrictive: you may add new rules or mark existing rules strict, but you cannot remove rules or turn strict mode off.

The Attention Firewall accessibility service observes foreground apps, window content, and supported browser address text so it can enforce your rules. Device Admin uninstall friction and notifications are optional. Rules, settings, and usage counters stay on-device. Configuration export includes the configured cooldown and deactivation-confirmation-period durations, but excludes the recovery key, active-protection state, pending deactivation request and timestamps, current allowance balance, usage counters, and temporary approvals. Import is unavailable while protection is active and cannot restore a pending request. Purpose text entered at the gate is not stored.

The default deactivation policy is a 24-hour cooldown followed by a 1-hour confirmation period. Cooldown choices are 0, 1 minute, 6 hours, 12 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, or 72 hours; confirmation-period choices are 1, 2, 3, 6, 12, or 24 hours. These settings can be changed only while protection is inactive. With a positive cooldown, enter the recovery key once to request deactivation. Protection and uninstall friction remain active while waiting. You can cancel the request immediately without the key. The confirmation period begins and expires silently: there is no notification, sound, vibration, badge, background polling, or automatic deactivation. During this period, enter the key again, press Deactivate protection, and accept the final confirmation. Incorrect keys do not change the deadline. If the confirmation period expires, the complete process must be restarted. Eligibility uses monotonic device time; a detected clock shift over two minutes or a reboot invalidates the request. With cooldown 0, one correct key, an explicit button press, and final confirmation deactivate without creating a request. Critical emergency and device-recovery apps cannot be selected for protection. Optional Device Admin and accessibility-based uninstall protection add friction, not kiosk-mode guarantees.
